questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Economic and Non-Economic Activities' refers to.
questions.a: Activities that create monetary value, like making furniture or flying planes, are economic activities; work done out of love or duty without payment, like teaching neighbourhood kids for free, is non-economic activity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Economic and Non-Economic Activities'.
questions.a: Money is the dividing line: the same skill, paid or unpaid, moves from market to service.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Economic and Non-Economic Activities', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: economic = work + payment; non_economic = work without payment

concepts.title: The Value of Work: Dignity in Every Task

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Value of Work: Dignity in Every Task' refers to.
questions.a: Every kind of honest work has worth, paid or unpaid; Swami Vivekananda's advice to do one's work as worship, and the respect owed to farmers, drivers, homema-kers and soldiers alike, ground this value.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Value of Work: Dignity in Every Task'.
questions.a: Work's worth is not measured by salary alone: effort, skill and service give every task dignity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Value of Work: Dignity in Every Task' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Value of work (source: fees113.txt, Value of work)

questions.q: Using the method 'Adding Value: Rajesh the Carpenter', work with: material_cost = 5000, selling_price = 5000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of value_added.

Take the relation taught for 'Adding Value: Rajesh the Carpenter' and work with: material_cost = 8000, selling_price = 80000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of value_added.
Explain in your own words what 'Adding Value: Rajesh the Carpenter' refers to.
questions.a: Rajesh buys wood for 600 rupees and sells each chair for 1,000; the extra 400 rupees is the monetary value his skill, time and effort added, which is exactly what makes his work an economic activity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Adding Value: Rajesh the Carpenter'.
questions.a: Value added is the measure of work: raw material in, a more valuable product out.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Adding Value: Rajesh the Carpenter', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Work beyond Money' refers to.
questions.a: The chapter honours work that payment cannot measure: a retired BSF grandfather teaching free geography classes, tending the vegetable garden, running errands, and homema-kers' daily care that holds a family together.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Work beyond Money'.
questions.a: A society runs on unpriced work too: care, teaching and service build the same wealth of trust.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Work beyond Money' taught, and from which source text?
